cistopic.corpus: No upstream checkpoint or pretraining corpus; each fit may contain only declared outer-training donor ATAC rows.

interpretation: cisTopic 0.3.0 has no upstream biological-corpus contamination because it is trained locally. Its dominant leakage risks are donor-spanning peak definition, region filtering, topic-count selection, joint fitting, label/prototype fitting, and model selection. More importantly, the pinned R release is transductive and exposes no inductive held-cell transform. It therefore cannot produce a valid held-donor score and cannot enter the current RNA-only held-back tasks.
remaining_blockers: Create a separate nonpromotable development-only ATAC TaskSpec before any fit; freeze rows, donor grouping, region inventory, metrics, model-selection rule, baselines, and the explicit absence of a champion claim.

Resolve whether a scientifically faithful independently audited inductive implementation exists. Do not silently substitute pycisTopic or append/refit held cells under the cisTopic 0.3.0 registry identity.

Activate each dataset only after donor, topology, native-reference, fragment, peak-coordinate, QC, rights, and missingness contracts pass. Preserve GSE244832 as same-sample different aliquot rather than cell-paired.
Freeze topic grid, WarpLDA settings, five seeds, training-only selection criterion, any downstream head, and every local artifact hash.
Reconstruct and validate the deprecated R 0.3.0 dependency closure on a SLURM CPU node and record R sessionInfo(), BLAS/thread details, determinism, memory, and runtime.
Reject external serialized R objects; admit only project-generated, checksummed artifacts whose classes, dimensions, row IDs, finite values, nonnegativity, and probability sums pass validation.
